verbatim_request: What does the wallet-report-card-app artifact do? Describe its UI, report-card logic, and what data it shows.

diagnosis.summary: Wallet Report Card is a read-only NFT wallet grading dashboard: enter any public EVM wallet address, pick Base, Ethereum, or Robinhood Chain, and it fetches the wallet's full ERC-721 transfer history (Blockscout REST, with a JSON-RPC log-scan fallback on Robinhood Chain), pairs acquisitions to exits into holding cycles, and issues a 0–100 score via the formula round(50 × min(avgHoldDays/365, 1) + 30 × (1 − 7d flip rate) + 20 × (1 − 30d flip rate)) with labels from Diamond Hands (80+) down to Paper Hands (<35). The UI shows a typographic score stamp, hold/flip metrics, a score-anatomy breakdown, the exact formula, and a copyable X-ready receipt; it refuses to score when history is missing, incomplete, or too large rather than inventing data. Nothing is connected or signed, and nothing is persisted — each scan is a fresh live fetch.
direct_observations: The landing page (confirmed by screenshot + aria snapshot) shows: mono kicker 'ERC-721 HOLDING ANALYSIS', serif headline 'How strong are those hands?', deck copy 'Trace a wallet's NFT exits, hold times, and flip patterns—then turn the history into one inspectable score.'

The scan card is a dark panel (olive-green accent button) containing a 'Wallet address' text input (placeholder '0x…', hint 'Any public EVM wallet. Nothing is connected or signed.'), a chain select ('Base — Blockscout', 'Ethereum — Blockscout', 'Robinhood Chain — Explorer + RPC fallback'), and a 'Grade this wallet' button disabled until a 42-char 0x address is entered.
Below the form sits a three-column 'How the rating works' primer: 50 points for average hold duration / 30 for avoiding 7-day flips / 20 for avoiding 30-day flips.

A scored report renders: a circular conic-gradient score stamp (score × 3.6°), the rating label, 'Scored from N acquisition cycles across M distinct NFTs', a 'Holding behavior' metric sheet, a 'Score anatomy' panel with three formula bars (Hold duration /50, 7-day discipline /30, 30-day discipline /20), a collapsible exact formula, an 'X-ready receipt' pre block with Copy button, and a footer with data source + check timestamp.

Four non-scored states exist: loading ('Building the full transfer timeline'), scan-failed with retry, 'NO SCORE ISSUED' (source unavailable or history >1,000 transfers), 'NO HISTORY' empty state, and 'EARLY READ' insufficient-history state (shows acquisition count, current holdings, oldest hold, and days until the first eligible 30-day read).
The score label tiers are 80–100 Diamond Hands, 60–79 Steady Holder, 35–59 Active Flipper, 0–34 Paper Hands (code `ratingFor` in actions.ts, echoed in the UI's formula details).

The UI carries an honest caveat: 'A transfer feed cannot prove a sale. Flip and time to sell use the first outbound transfer after acquisition as a transparent proxy; gifts and wallet moves can affect the result.'

Data sources per DATA-PLAN.md: Base and Ethereum via Blockscout REST (probed live, HTTP 200, 50 items/page, next_page_params pagination, max 20 pages); Robinhood Chain via its Blockscout first, falling back to public JSON-RPC eth_getLogs Transfer-topic scans (chain id 0x1237 verified) with recursive range-splitting on the provider's 10,000-log limit.
No user history is persisted: server actions hold no DB tables for scans, the isolated capture contains only `__drizzle_migrations`, and each Scan is a fresh live fetch whose results render once.
source_derived_hypotheses: Hypothesis (not observed in this inspection): the live scan path should still work end-to-end today, since all external sources were live-probed during the build and the server action fails closed on any source failure; the captured audit only rendered the landing form and never submitted a scan.
Hypothesis: Robinhood Chain scans most likely resolve via the JSON-RPC fallback today, because DATA-PLAN.md records the Robinhood Blockscout host returning Cloudflare challenge HTML at build time.

Hypothesis: very large wallets (e.g. high-volume flippers with >1,000 ERC-721 transfers or >20 Blockscout pages) will hit the intentional 'history exceeds the safe scan limit' error rather than a partial score — by design, but unobserved here.

cause.summary: The artifact is a read-only, fail-closed NFT wallet grading dashboard: one server action scans a wallet's full ERC-721 transfer history on Base, Ethereum, or Robinhood Chain and converts hold times plus 7-day/30-day flip behavior into an inspectable 0–100 score with a Diamond Hands → Paper Hands label. Everything shown is computed live from chain data at scan time; the app explicitly refuses to guess, sample, or persist anything.
evidence: Server source `server/src/actions.ts` implements the full transfer-history pipeline: Blockscout ERC-721 transfer pagination for Base/Ethereum, Robinhood Blockscout first with public JSON-RPC Transfer-log fallback, oldest-first cycle pairing, flip-rate denominators, and the exact 50/30/20 scoring formula.

Client source `client/src/App.tsx` renders the scan form, all five response states (ok / no_history / insufficient_history / error / client error), the score stamp, metric rows, score-anatomy formula bars, and the X-ready receipt.

`DATA-PLAN.md` documents live-tested sources (Base/Ethereum Blockscout 200s, Robinhood Cloudflare 403 rejection, RPC chain id 0x1237) and the fail-closed contract: never invent data, no sample wallets.

Render capture aria snapshot + full-page screenshot confirm the landing UI: headline 'How strong are those hands?', wallet address input, chain combobox (Base/Ethereum/Robinhood), disabled-until-valid 'Grade this wallet' button, and the 50/30/20 'How the rating works' primer.
The app publishes exactly one server action, `analyzewallet` (artifact.list_actions), and the isolated data layer contains only `__drizzle_migrations` — no wallet history is persisted anywhere.

unavailable_evidence: No live scan result was captured in this inspection: the audit only rendered the landing form, so the correctness of a real end-to-end analysis against current chain data was not observed.
The Robinhood Chain Blockscout-vs-RPC fallback path was not re-verified live in this inspection; the Cloudflare 403 behavior is documented in DATA-PLAN.md from build-time probes only.

Published action request schema for `analyzewallet` was not fetched via artifact.list_actions action_name (list confirmed the single action exists); the request/response shape was instead read directly from the Zod schemas in server/src/actions.ts.
preservation_requirements: There is no persisted user data to preserve: the app stores no wallet scans, no history, and no user accounts — the only data is migration metadata.
Preserve the fail-closed contract: any modification must keep 'no invented data' behavior (no sample wallets, no estimated metrics, no scores without complete paginated history).
Preserve the read-only security posture: no wallet connection, no signatures, no approvals — the action takes only an address string and a chain enum.
diagnosis.recommended_modification: No modification is required by this report — the artifact is complete, audited clean (HTTP 200, no console errors, no broken assets, mobile layout pass), and matches its DATA-PLAN contract. If iterated on later, an optional polish would be to include the flip-rate eligible-cycle denominators (e.g. '3/41 cycles') inside the X-ready receipt so the shared text is as auditable as the on-page formula bars — this is cosmetic only and changes no logic.
